name: Zabeel Park
description: Large green park with playgrounds, a boating lake and shaded lawns. Very low cost and easy for young children.

name: Safa Park
description: Classic Dubai park with wide lawns, play areas and a jogging track. Good low-cost break between paid attractions.

name: Creek Park
description: Waterfront park along Dubai Creek with playgrounds, gardens and a cable car. Popular family picnic spot.

name: Al Barsha Pond Park
description: Free neighbourhood park circling a pond, with a running track and children's play areas. Ideal budget filler.

name: Mushrif Park
description: Sprawling desert park with pools, cycling trails and shaded barbecue areas. Half-day option for active families.

name: Al Mamzar Beach Park
description: Beach park with sheltered swimming lagoons, lawns and playgrounds. Combines a park and a safe beach for kids.

name: Quranic Park
description: Free themed park with a glass botanical house and cave of miracles. Quiet, educational and shaded.

name: Dubai Miracle Garden
description: Seasonal flower garden with enormous floral sculptures. Photogenic, pleasant in cooler months, closed in summer.

name: Children's City
description: Indoor edutainment centre for under-12s with hands-on science exhibits. Air-conditioned midday option.

name: Aquaventure Waterpark
description: Huge waterpark at Atlantis with record-breaking slides, a lazy river and a private beach. Best for teens and confident swimmers.

name: Wild Wadi Waterpark
description: Waterpark beneath Burj Al Arab with a wave pool and gentle kids' zone alongside steeper slides.

name: Laguna Waterpark
description: Mid-sized waterpark at La Mer with a surf zone and toddler splash area. Cheaper alternative to the big two.

name: IMG Worlds of Adventure
description: Largest indoor theme park in the world, with Marvel and dinosaur zones. Fully air-conditioned — a summer standby.

name: Motiongate Dubai
description: Hollywood-themed park with coasters and studio shows. Long day out; best for teens and older children.

name: Legoland Dubai
description: Theme park built for 2–12 year olds, with gentle rides and Miniland. The strongest young-kid full-day option.

name: Legoland Water Park
description: Shallow, gentle water park designed for young children, with build-a-raft rivers. No height-limit thrill slides.

name: Museum of the Future
description: Immersive future-themed museum inside Dubai's calligraphy-clad torus. Strong with teens; book timed entry.

name: Etihad Museum
description: Museum on the founding of the UAE, built around the 1971 union house. Cheap, cool and quick to visit.

name: Dubai Museum at Al Fahidi Fort
description: City museum inside the oldest fort in Dubai, with dioramas of pearl-diving life. Almost free.

name: Al Shindagha Museum
description: Restored creekside houses telling Dubai's perfume, pearl and trading history across many small pavilions.

name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
description: Free-to-wander wind-tower quarter of coral-stone lanes, galleries and courtyard cafés. Lovely at dusk.

name: Coffee Museum
description: Tiny museum of coffee history in Al Fahidi with tastings. A cheap, short filler between bigger stops.

name: Alserkal Avenue
description: Warehouse district of free contemporary art galleries and independent cafés. Adult-leaning and air-conditioned.

name: Dubai Frame
description: Giant picture-frame viewpoint with a glass walkway between old and new Dubai. Quick, cheap and dramatic.

name: Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo
description: Giant mall aquarium with a tunnel walk-through and underwater zoo. Indoor — a good midday option for young kids.

name: The Green Planet
description: Indoor bio-dome rainforest with sloths, birds and reptiles at close range. Compact and very popular with children.

name: Dubai Safari Park
description: Large open-range safari park with African and Asian villages. Cheap for what it is; closed through high summer.

name: The Lost Chambers Aquarium
description: Atlantis aquarium themed as sunken ruins, with rays and sharks in vast tanks. Cool, calm and indoors.

name: Dubai Butterfly Garden
description: Climate-controlled domes filled with thousands of butterflies. Short, gentle and reliably delightful for small children.

name: Dubai Crocodile Park
description: Indoor crocodile habitat with feeding talks and a small aquarium wing. Air-conditioned and stroller-friendly.

name: JBR The Beach
description: Free public beach backed by a promenade of cafés and cinemas. Lifeguarded and busy — good all-ages filler.

name: Kite Beach
description: Free active beach with kitesurfing, volleyball and a food truck strip. Popular with teens and young adults.

name: La Mer Beach
description: Free beachfront with murals, splash pads and casual restaurants. Works as either a cheap stop or an evening stroll.

name: Jumeirah Public Beach
description: Quiet stretch of free public sand with showers and lifeguards. Reliable zero-cost relief valve on a tight budget.

name: Umm Suqeim Beach
description: Free beach with the classic Burj Al Arab view. Best at sunset; a romantic no-cost evening option.

name: Black Palace Beach
description: Secluded unfacilitated beach between palaces, popular for quiet sunsets. No lifeguards — supervise children.

name: Al Mamzar Corniche
description: Free waterfront walkway with sea views and shaded benches. A cheap, calm way to close a day.

name: XLine Dubai Marina
description: Urban zipline flying over Dubai Marina. Strict age and weight limits — teens and adults only.

name: Skydive Dubai
description: Tandem skydive over the Palm. Adults only and very expensive — a splurge line item, not a default.

name: Al Marmoom Desert Safari
description: Evening desert safari with dune drive, camel ride and barbecue dinner under the stars. Runs late afternoon into night.

name: Hatta Kayak
description: Kayaking on the turquoise Hatta Dam between mountains. Cheap, scenic and doable from about age six.

name: Ski Dubai
description: Indoor ski slope and snow park inside Mall of the Emirates, with penguin encounters. The strongest summer-heat escape.

name: Hot Air Balloon Dubai
description: Sunrise balloon flight over the desert conservation reserve. Very early start; memorable and romantic.

name: Al Fanar Restaurant & Cafe
description: Traditional Emirati restaurant styled as a 1960s Dubai home. Relaxed, family-friendly and mid-priced.

name: Ravi Restaurant
description: Legendary no-frills Pakistani canteen in Satwa. Extremely cheap and open almost around the clock.

name: Arabian Tea House
description: Turquoise-benched courtyard café in Al Fahidi serving Emirati breakfasts. Shaded and pretty.

name: Bu Qtair
description: Beachside fried-fish shack with a cult following and a queue. Cheap, fresh and unfussy.

name: Logma
description: Modern Emirati comfort food and karak chai inside Dubai Mall. Convenient between mall-area attractions.

name: Operation Falafel
description: Fast, cheap Levantine street food in JBR. Good quick lunch when the budget is tight.

name: SALT Kite Beach
description: Beachside burger truck that grew into an institution. Quick, cheap and a teen favourite.

name: Zaroob
description: Bright street-food-style Levantine diner on Sheikh Zayed Road. Cheap and open very late.

name: Al Ustad Special Kabab
description: Bur Dubai institution serving Iranian kebabs since 1978, walls covered in photographs. Cheap and characterful.

name: Karak House
description: Casual karak-and-breakfast spot with Emirati snacks. Very cheap; useful as a short first slot of the day.

name: Ibn AlBahr
description: Lebanese seafood on a Palm boardwalk with skyline views. Family-friendly but pleasant for couples too.

name: Pierchic
description: Overwater fine-dining restaurant on a pier with sunset views. A signature anniversary venue.

name: At.mosphere Burj Khalifa
description: Dining on the 122nd floor of the Burj Khalifa. Dress code and reservation required; spectacular at night.

name: Ossiano
description: Underwater tasting-menu restaurant set against the Atlantis aquarium wall. Long, theatrical and expensive.

name: Zuma Dubai
description: Contemporary Japanese izakaya in DIFC, buzzing and stylish. Popular for celebratory adult dinners.

name: 101 Dining Lounge & Marina
description: Mediterranean dining on a Palm jetty reached by boat, facing the Marina skyline. Sunset slot is the one to book.

name: Al Mahara
description: Seafood restaurant inside Burj Al Arab wrapped around a floor-to-ceiling aquarium. Formal and very expensive.

name: Sea Fu Restaurant
description: Asian seafood on the sand with skyline views. Torch-lit and quiet in the evening.

name: Trèsind Studio
description: Twenty-course modern Indian tasting menu at a chef's counter. A long, special-occasion evening.

name: The Dubai Mall
description: Vast air-conditioned mall with an aquarium, ice rink and fountain views. The default midday heat fallback.

name: Mall of the Emirates
description: Major mall wrapped around Ski Dubai, with a cinema and food halls. Free to enter and reliably cool.

name: Ibn Battuta Mall
description: Themed mall with courts styled after Ibn Battuta's travels. Interesting to walk through even without shopping.

name: City Walk
description: Open-air retail and dining district that comes alive in the evening. Free to wander.

name: Global Village
description: Seasonal cultural festival park with country pavilions, funfair rides and street food. Evenings only, October to April.

name: The Dubai Fountain
description: Free choreographed fountain show on Burj Lake, every half hour after dark. A classic free evening slot.

name: Dhow Dinner Cruise Marina
description: Two-hour dinner cruise through Dubai Marina on a traditional dhow. Fixed departure time.

name: La Perle by Dragone
description: Resident aqua-theatre show with divers and acrobatics. Fixed showtimes; book ahead.

name: Dubai Creek Abra Ride
description: Traditional wooden abra crossing Dubai Creek for a couple of dirhams. The cheapest memorable thing in the city.

name: Umm Al Emarat Park
description: Family park with shaded playgrounds, a small animal barn and a botanic garden. Ideal for children under 10; very low cost.

name: Khalifa Park
description: Large park with canals, a miniature train and playgrounds. Cheap and easy with a stroller.

name: Family Park Corniche
description: Free seafront park on the Corniche with play areas and shaded lawns. Useful zero-cost slot.

name: Al Bateen Park
description: Quiet free neighbourhood park with modern play equipment and a walking loop.

name: Yas Gateway Park
description: Free green space on Yas Island with cycle paths. Handy cheap break between the island's paid parks.

name: Delma Park
description: Small free city park with a fenced playground. Good short stop for toddlers.

name: Yas Waterworld
description: Large waterpark with 40+ rides from kids' splash zones to high-adrenaline slides. Best for teens and older kids.

name: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
description: Indoor theme park with the world's fastest roller coaster. Loud and fast — a teen magnet.

name: Warner Bros World Abu Dhabi
description: Fully indoor park themed on Looney Tunes and DC. Gentler than Ferrari World and excellent in summer.

name: SeaWorld Abu Dhabi
description: Indoor marine life park with a vast aquarium and research centre. Strong for animal-loving children.

name: CLYMB Abu Dhabi
description: Indoor skydiving flight chamber and the region's tallest climbing wall. Teen-focused and air-conditioned.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
description: Landmark museum under a floating steel dome of light. Free for under-18s, which makes it very budget-efficient.

name: Qasr Al Watan
description: Working presidential palace open to visitors, with a vast domed hall and evening light show.

name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
description: Free-to-visit white marble mosque, extraordinary at dusk. Modest dress required; book a time slot.

name: Qasr Al Hosn
description: The city's oldest stone building, now a museum of Abu Dhabi's history. Cheap and cool.

name: Founder's Memorial
description: Free memorial garden built around a monumental suspended portrait. Best after sunset when it is lit.

name: Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital
description: Guided tour of a working falcon hospital where you can hold a falcon. Morning slots only; book ahead.

name: The National Aquarium Abu Dhabi
description: The region's largest aquarium, with a walk-through ocean tunnel and penguin zone. Indoors and stroller-friendly.

name: Emirates Park Zoo
description: Mid-sized zoo with giraffe feeding and a petting barn. Affordable and very popular with young children.

name: Al Ain Zoo
description: Large zoo and safari at the foot of Jebel Hafeet. Excellent value; a long drive from the coast.

name: Corniche Beach
description: Blue-flag city beach with lifeguards, shaded play areas and a long promenade. Almost free.

name: Saadiyat Public Beach
description: Protected natural beach with soft sand and nesting turtles. Cheap entry with showers and loungers.

name: Yas Beach
description: Relaxed beach club on Yas Island with kayaks and paddleboards. Convenient after a morning at the theme parks.

name: Al Bateen Beach
description: Calm family beach with a shallow swimming area and a splash park. Very cheap.

name: Jubail Mangrove Park
description: Boardwalk through mangrove wetlands with birdlife and interpretation panels. Cheap, shaded and easy on legs.

name: Mangrove Kayak Tour
description: Guided kayak through the mangrove channels, including sunset departures. Minimum age eight.

name: Al Khatim Desert Safari
description: Afternoon-to-night desert safari with dune bashing, camels and a camp dinner.

name: Jebel Hafeet Summit Drive
description: Free drive up a famous switchback mountain road to a summit viewpoint. Spectacular at sunset.

name: Hudayriyat Adventure Park
description: Outdoor adventure hub with ropes courses, ziplines and a skate park. Built for energetic older kids and teens.

name: Al Mrzab Restaurant
description: Homely Emirati restaurant known for machboos and harees. Cheap and generous.

name: Bait El Khetyar
description: Popular Lebanese grill and breakfast house. Very affordable and open early.

name: Shawarma Time
description: Cheap shawarma counter with a loyal late-night following. The lowest-cost meal slot available.

name: Yas Marina Waterfront Cafe
description: Marina-side café convenient to the Yas Island parks. Reliable mid-priced lunch stop.

name: Emirati Kitchen
description: Modern take on Emirati home cooking, with tasting platters good for sharing.

name: Beirut Restaurant
description: Long-running Lebanese mezze house with outdoor seating. Comfortable for a longer family dinner.

name: Al Dhafra Fish Restaurant
description: Harbourside seafood restaurant where you pick the catch. Mid-priced and popular with locals.

name: Hakkasan Abu Dhabi
description: Michelin-pedigree Cantonese dining inside Emirates Palace. Dark, elegant and expensive.

name: Li Beirut
description: Refined Lebanese dining with sea views at Emirates Palace. A strong anniversary choice.

name: Talea by Antonio Guida
description: Contemporary Italian tasting menus overlooking Yas Marina. Quiet and adult-oriented.

name: Sontaya
description: South-East Asian dining in waterside timber pavilions on Saadiyat. Lantern-lit and secluded.

name: Villa Toscana
description: Tuscan courtyard restaurant with live music. Warm and celebratory rather than formal.

name: Yas Mall
description: Yas Island's mall, directly linked to Ferrari World. The natural cool-down between park visits.

name: Marina Mall Abu Dhabi
description: Seafront mall with a viewing tower and skating rink. Free entry and reliably cool.

name: The Galleria Al Maryah
description: Upscale island mall with a large dining terrace. Quiet on weekday afternoons.

name: Corniche Dhow Cruise
description: Evening dinner cruise along the Corniche skyline on a traditional dhow.

name: Emirates Palace Sunset Cruise
description: Private-charter sunset sail past Emirates Palace with canapés. Adults only and firmly romantic.

name: Qasr Al Watan Light Show
description: Projection-mapped light and sound show on the palace façade. Cheap, short and reliably impressive.

name: Yas Marina Race Night
description: Evening track experience at the Yas Marina Circuit. Fixed sessions; strong pull for teenagers.

name: Al Majaz Waterfront
description: Free lakeside promenade with splash pads, a musical fountain and cafés. Lively in the evening.

name: Al Noor Island
description: Landscaped island with a butterfly house and illuminated sculptures. Beautiful after dark.

name: Al Montazah Parks
description: Combined water park and amusement park at a fraction of the Dubai price. Strong budget substitute.

name: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilization
description: Well-curated museum of Islamic art and science in a restored souk building. Very cheap and cool.

name: Sharjah Art Museum
description: Free regional art museum with a strong Arab modernist collection. Quiet and air-conditioned.

name: Sharjah Aquarium
description: Compact aquarium of Gulf marine life next to the maritime museum. A fraction of Dubai Aquarium's price.

name: Al Khan Beach
description: Free family beach with calm shallow water and a walking path. Zero-cost relief valve.

name: Khorfakkan Beach
description: Free crescent beach on the east coast backed by mountains. Long drive but one of the best beaches in the country.

name: Mleiha Archaeological Centre
description: Desert archaeology centre with fossil-rock hikes and stargazing tours. Educational and genuinely striking.

name: Khorfakkan Waterfall Walk
description: Free man-made waterfall and amphitheatre set into the mountainside. Lit up in the evening.

name: Sadaf Restaurant
description: Long-standing Iranian grill near the corniche. Cheap, fast and consistently busy.

name: Bait Al Aleef
description: Emirati heritage restaurant in a restored courtyard house in the Heart of Sharjah.

name: Sharjah Fish Market Grill
description: Pick your fish at the market and have it grilled next door. Cheap and very local.

name: Sanabel Al Sharjah
description: Lakeside fine dining overlooking the Al Majaz fountain. The most affordable romantic option in the north.

name: City Centre Sharjah
description: Practical air-conditioned mall with a family entertainment centre. Free to enter.

name: Sharjah Light Festival
description: Free seasonal projection-mapping festival across the city's landmark façades. February only.

name: Eye of the Emirates
description: Sixty-metre observation wheel at Al Qasba with air-conditioned cabins. Cheap and quick.

name: Jebel Jais Flight Zipline
description: World's longest zipline. Strict age and weight limits; teens and adults only.

name: Jais Sledder
description: Longest mountain toboggan track in the world, ridable from age six. Far gentler than the zipline.

name: Jebel Jais Via Ferrata
description: Guided cliff-face climbing route with cable bridges. Strenuous; minimum age twelve.

name: Bear Grylls Explorers Camp
description: Survival-skills camp on Jebel Jais with abseiling and navigation sessions. Built for older kids and teens.

name: Al Hamra Beach
description: Long quiet stretch of free public beach with calm water. Good escape from Dubai crowds.

name: Al Marjan Island Beach
description: Free island beach with a sunset-facing promenade. Very quiet on weekdays.

name: Saqr Park
description: Family park with a miniature train, small rides and a skating rink. Almost free.

name: National Museum of Ras Al Khaimah
description: Small museum inside an eighteenth-century fort, covering pearling and archaeology. Costs almost nothing.

name: Puro Beach Al Hamra
description: Beach club restaurant with loungers and Mediterranean plates. Pleasant long lunch.

name: Nahaam
description: Beachfront seafood restaurant facing the sunset. Quiet and notably cheaper than Dubai equivalents.

name: Al Aqah Beach
description: Free east-coast beach facing Snoopy Island, with clear water and mountain backdrop.

name: Sandy Beach Fujairah
description: Day-pass beach with showers, loungers and easy snorkelling access. Cheap for a full afternoon.

name: Snoopy Island Snorkelling
description: Guided snorkelling around a rocky island with reef fish and turtles. Confident swimmers from age eight.

name: Wadi Wurayah Trek
description: Guided trek into a protected mountain wadi with rock pools. Strenuous; minimum age ten.

name: Fujairah Fort
description: Oldest fort in the UAE, with a restored heritage village beside it. Nearly free.

name: Ain Al Madhab Gardens
description: Mountain-spring garden park with pools and shaded picnic areas. Costs almost nothing.

name: Al Meshwar Restaurant
description: Landmark family restaurant in a castle-like building. Cheap grills and generous mezze.

name: Fujairah Sunset Dhow Cruise
description: Sunset dhow cruise along the Gulf of Oman coastline. Calmer and cheaper than the Dubai cruises.

name: Ajman Corniche Beach
description: Free white-sand city beach with a long promenade and play areas. Quiet and easy to reach.

name: Al Zorah Nature Reserve
description: Mangrove reserve with flamingos and kayak channels. Cheap, calm and good for early mornings.

name: Ajman Museum
description: Fort museum with pearling and archaeology displays. One of the cheapest indoor stops in the country.

name: Kuzbara
description: Casual Levantine kitchen on the corniche. Very affordable and open from breakfast.

name: Ajman Fish Market Grill
description: Buy fish at the market and have it grilled to order. Cheap and authentically local.

name: City Centre Ajman
description: Compact air-conditioned mall with a cinema and play zone. Free midday heat shelter.

name: Dreamland Aqua Park
description: Long-established water park with a huge range of slides at half the Dubai price. Strong budget substitute.

name: Umm Al Quwain Public Beach
description: Very quiet free beach with shallow water. Almost empty on weekdays.

name: UAQ Mangrove Kayak
description: Guided kayak through quiet mangrove creeks with birdlife. Cheapest kayaking in the country.

name: Al Sinnara Restaurant
description: Creekside seafood restaurant serving the day's catch. Inexpensive and unhurried.
